title: Puzzle 3D React Parity
description: Restore premigration parity for puzzle 3D in the React renderer: GLB coordinate frame, hover/select/gumball/marquee protocol, scene layers (vortices/attractions/target volumes/references/brush preview), and Select/Brush/Fill window engagements.
summary:
Fixed Brush and Fill in the puzzle 3d React app — both were fully dead per the user's report, confirmed via live repro. Root causes, all in the renderer/UI-kit contract (the plugin side was already correct and unit-tested):

**Fix 1 — Brush click selected the object instead of placing.** `WorldVortexMarkers.onPointerDown` (world-3d-host.tsx) didn't stopPropagation in brush mode, so pointerdown fell through to the instance mesh and selected/gumballed it instead of persisting the brush target; the async worldVortexHover round-trip could also clear the target before the click's onClick fired. Fixed by dispatching `worldVortexSelect` on pointer-down (persisting the target, mirroring the wgpu reference) and gating instance picking off entirely while brush/fill is active (`blockPick`). Root-fixed in the plugin too: `worldVortexHover` was overwriting `selection.vortex_ids` on every hover-out, silently destroying a real selection — split into a separate `hovered_vortex_full_id` field. Extracted the pointer-decision logic into pure, tested helpers (`worldInstancePickBlocked`, `resolveVortexPointerDownIntent`, `brushObjectPlacementArgs`) since R3F/WebGL can't be exercised in the existing test harness. Verified live: hover shows the ghost + candidate picker, click places the object (object/attraction counts increment), no accidental selection, Select-mode picking still works correctly (regression-checked).

**Fix 2 — Engagement command line silently ate multi-word commands.** The React shell PascalCases and strips all separators from typed drafts (`normalizeEngagementActionText`) before submitting — "fill 20" arrives as "Fill20", not "fill 20" — but puzzle d3's `engagementSubmit` parser used `to_lowercase()+split_whitespace()`, so it never matched. Added a shared `strip_engagement_prefix`/`engagement_token_matches` helper (framework/plugin/rs/lib.rs) implementing the same contract cad's `parse_repl_line` already relies on, and used it to fix the same bug in layout (export commands), writer (font/tab/line-numbers), and lowpoly (its typed-action-id shorthand, which was actually broken for every camelCase action since day one). Verified live: `fill 20` via the command line places 20 objects end-to-end.

**Fix 3 — Fill count silently stayed 0.** `setFillCount` parsed with `.as_u64()`, which returns `None` for a JSON float (`20.0`) sent across the wasm bridge — fixed to `.as_f64()` (matching the sibling `setVoxelDims`), and applied the same fix to puzzle 2d and 5d's identical `setFillCount` handlers.

**Also fixed**, an unrelated compile break hit while verifying (pre-existing/concurrent, needed to unblock the final build): `framework/core/rs/lib.rs` was mid-refactor missing an import for `framework_panel_tab_label` — added it.

**Follow-ups flagged as separate background tasks** (real, scoped, verified-but-out-of-scope issues found during this pass, not caused by today's fixes):
- The shared engagement Slider control (ui/js/react/index.tsx) doesn't respond to drag or keyboard arrows at all — confirmed via a clean isolated repro where Radix's own `onValueChange` never fires. Affects every plugin using slider-kind controls, not just puzzle 3d.
- Puzzle 3d's direct object-drag gesture (`worldRelocate`) is fully implemented and tested plugin-side but was never wired up in the React host — only gumball-handle dragging currently works.

**Part 2 — premigration parity audit**: code-reviewed (and live-spot-checked select/marquee/keybindings) every remaining feature from the original 12-phase parity ticket against the premigration app — precompute driving, marquee select, Ctrl-A/Escape keybindings, right-click context menu, worldRelocate's attraction re-derivation, undo/redo, kinds catalogue, hierarchy hide/lock, inspector edits, view presets, OBJ/GLB export. All confirmed wired with matching action names and existing test coverage; no additional gaps found beyond the two flagged above.

Tests: puzzle-plugin 156/157 pass (1 pre-existing unrelated failure in d2 camera-geometry, confirmed unaffected by this work), framework-plugin 20/20, layout 34/34, writer 30/30, lowpoly 34/34, react renderer full suite green (89 tests, up from 81).
